In particular, it addresses the questions exhausted new Indian parents face: when people may visit, how long they should stay, and why they should not kiss the baby. I have also included checklists, Do's & Don'ts tables, and anecdotes.

Because I am preparing my debut book, I would appreciate your help refining it into something readers will enjoy and publishing it successfully as a paperback.

Could you advise me on the following?
1\. What process should we follow?
2\. What would the price and timeline be?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
While preparing the final version, I’ll carefully review the highlighted sections as well, so no worries there. Thank you for reviewing the manuscript and accepting the edits.

Here are my responses to your questions:

1\. The sentence "So, I used to eat before anyone or sometimes after everytime, basically it was on demand." does not sound grammatically natural. To preserve your meaning while making the passage flow more smoothly, I recommend:

"So, I ate whenever I was hungry. Sometimes I ate before everyone else, and sometimes afterwards. My meals were completely on demand."

2\. You're absolutely right about the current wording: instead of recounting what you actually experienced, it sounds as though you wished those things had happened. Because this is your own story, I suggest describing the completed actions directly:

"The thing I needed most from my partner was not grand gestures. He answered the door when visitors arrived. He made sure my water bottle was always filled and within my reach. Sometimes he would simply check in on me, give me a hug, or put a blanket over me. He managed the visitors so I didn't have to. They were small acts, but they meant everything."

That version makes it clear that your partner really did those things for you.

1\. My honest view is that the manuscript was genuinely enjoyable to read. You have covered a subject that is not discussed enough, particularly in Indian families. The writing is warm, relatable, and accessible, and many new parents are likely to recognize their own experiences in it. My only suggestion would be to tighten some repetitive sections in a future edition. Overall, it is a lovely and genuinely useful book.

2\. Regarding images, I would personally keep them minimal. A few simple illustrations or icons at chapter openings could work well, but I would avoid adding too many. The writing should remain the main focus, while a clean, elegant layout will give the book a more professional appearance.
